note: Triennial election of Down County Council, polled Thursday 4 June 1936 (Belfast News-Letter, 13 April 1936, p. 10). There were no contests. The Northern Whig of 9 May 1936 (p. 8) lists the twenty members who 'will comprise the new County Council', without divisions; each division is taken from the 1933 return or from the 1936 reports of the three changes (Bangor, Garvaghy, Portaferry: Belfast News-Letter, 7 May 1936, p. 15; Dromore Leader, 9 May 1936, p. 2) and Comber (J. M. Andrews's election notice, Northern Whig, 8 May 1936). No one was nominated for Dromore, where the retiring member, W. Liddell, was declared re-elected; he resigned and James Ervine was co-opted (round 2, 7 Nov 2026). New member, succeeding Walter Malcolm. Addresses and occupations printed with the names are not reproduced (privacy rule; gap-fill 6 Nov 2026). Returned unopposed.
